ledger.text: The sleep framework: A new way for LLMs to retain knowledge in continual learning

We introduce a sleep phase in continual learning, enabling large language models to continuously integrate new facts and enhance reasoning while mitigating catastrophic forgetting or static knowledge cutoffs.

Inspired by how the human brain processes and stabilizes memory during rest, we introduce a sleep framework in continual learning: a learning paradigm that equips large language models (LLMs) with a continuous periodic lifecycle, enabling them to continually learn, consolidate…

With this framework, we demonstrate that alternating between active interaction and offline memory consolidation allows LLMs to continuously acquire new facts, retain long-context knowledge up to 10M tokens, and improve complex reasoning.
In a continual learning framework, this distinction becomes artificial; an intelligent agent must constantly learn, adapt, and process information.

This is achieved through Generalized Knowledge Distillation (GKD) combined with reinforcement learning (RL)-based imitation learning : • On-policy distillation: The expanded student model learns token-specific feedback from teacher distributions generated on self-sampled seque…

Overview of our sleep framework: Input streams from the active phase are stored in short-term memory before entering the sleep cycle, which bifurcates into Consolidation (transferring fragile short-term tokens into expanded long-term parametric memory using low-rank structures…

Beyond the empirical results, our sleep paradigm is grounded in a theory that clarifies why its two stages (memory consolidation and dreaming) can support continual learning without simply trading new knowledge for old capabilities.
